titleEn: One: Oar. Two: Vest. Three: Bread!

pages.text: Today they were going by boat to Grandpa's house! Pongi hopped into the tied-up boat. "Dad, hurry aboard!" From the bank, Dad, in his overalls, asked, "Have you packed everything?" "Yes! All ready!" said Pongi.

Dad looked over the side into the boat. There was just a bare wooden floor. "Oh? The boat looks empty." Pongi had been so excited that she forgot to pack. "We only have to untie the rope!" she pouted.
Dad pointed to the boat from the bank. "Where can the boat go without an oar?" The tied-up boat only rocked gently in its place. "Oh... it can't go." Pongi's mouth drooped.
Dad knelt on the bank and looked Pongi in the eyes. "It's easy not to forget things. Count as you load them, one by one. Shall we try together?" He held up one paw.

Dad laid an oar, a vest, and a basket of bread side by side on the bank. "These three will get us to Grandpa's house." Pongi pointed to each. "Oar, vest, bread!" Her little brother held his shell. "Bread!"
Dad lowered his voice. "Shall we load them one at a time?" Pongi put the oar on the boat floor. "One, oar!" The vest and bread basket were still on the bank.

Pongi set the bread basket beside the vest. On the boat floor were the oar, the vest, and the bread, all in a row. She called with Dad, "One, oar! Two, vest! Three, bread!" Her brother waved his shell. "Bread!"
Pongi put on the vest and took the oar. Dad untied the boat. "Nothing's missing! Now we can go!" Pongi thumped her tail on the boat floor. The boat glided forward.
Another day, when they were going to Grandpa's house, Pongi loaded all three things onto the boat floor. "One, oar! Two, vest! Three, bread!" The boat was ready before Dad even came down to the bank.

Dad lifted Pongi onto his shoulders. "You're the boat-packing captain, Pongi!" Count and load things one by one, and nothing gets left out. "One, oar! Two, vest! Three, bread! Let's get aboard!" Pongi called from his shoulders.
